issues.detail: The Greek 'ζων' (living) is an adjective/participle modifying the subject, but the Vietnamese 'khi còn sống' (while still alive) shifts the meaning to a temporal clause. The Greek phrase 'ζων μετα τρεις ημερας εγειρομαι' means 'I will rise [from the dead] alive after three days' (or simply 'I will rise after three days'), whereas the Vietnamese implies he said it *during* his life. Furthermore, the Greek 'εγειρομαι' is a present tense used as a future, but the Vietnamese 'sẽ sống lại' correctly captures the future intent; however, the 'ζων' placement is the primary fidelity issue.
